# usePointerPosition

> Pointer coordinates over the window or an element, throttled to one update per animation frame.

🟡 intermediate · React 16.8+ · Custom Hooks › Device & preferences · support: client-only

**Playground:** `npm run dev` → [`#/entry/use-pointer-position`](http://localhost:5173/#/entry/use-pointer-position)

## Concept

A passive `pointermove` listener stores the latest event; a single `requestAnimationFrame` per frame turns it into `{ clientX, clientY, x, y, ratioX, ratioY, pointerType }`.

## Problem

`setState` on every `pointermove` can mean hundreds of renders per second — more than the screen can display — and janky interactions.

## When to use

- Cursor-following UI, custom crosshairs, parallax, drawing previews, tooltips that follow the pointer.

## When not to use

- Purely visual following effects with no React state needed — write to a DOM style in the listener (or a CSS variable) and skip React renders entirely.
- Drag-and-drop with pointer capture — use a dedicated library or `setPointerCapture` handlers.

## API

```ts
function usePointerPosition(options?: {
  target?: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>;
  enabled?: boolean;
}): PointerPosition | null;
```

| Parameter                      | Type                             | Description                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------ | -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `options.target` _(optional)_  | `RefObject<HTMLElement \| null>` | Track inside this element (coordinates relative to it; resets on `pointerleave`). Default: window. |
| `options.enabled` _(optional)_ | `boolean`                        | Pause tracking (default `true`). The last value is kept.                                           |

**Returns:** `null` until the first move, then the latest position.

## Execution flow

1. Effect: resolves the target (ref is read after commit) and adds a passive `pointermove` listener.
2. Event: stores the event; schedules one rAF if none is pending.
3. Frame: reads `getBoundingClientRect()` once and commits one state update.
4. Cleanup: removes listeners and cancels a pending frame.

## Common mistakes

### Rendering on every event

❌ Incorrect:

```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  const onMove = (e: PointerEvent) => setPos({ x: e.clientX, y: e.clientY });
  window.addEventListener('pointermove', onMove);
  return () => window.removeEventListener('pointermove', onMove);
}, []);
```

High-frequency pointers (and 120 Hz displays) trigger far more renders than frames.

## Edge cases

- Touch only produces moves while the finger is down, and scrolling may claim the gesture — set `touch-action: none` on the element.
- A ref target that mounts later is attached when `enabled` or `target` changes.

## Browser support

Returns `null` on the server and until the first move.

## Testing
